t: You're standing on Villiers Street, which links the Strand with the Embankment. It's partly pedestrianised, and traffic runs northbound only. Nicholas Barbon built it in the 1670s on the site of York House, the property of George Villiers, Duke of Buckingham, whom the street commemorates. Buckingham was a courtier and statesman, a notable patron of the arts, and a favourite of King James the First. A watergate in nearby Embankment Gardens is the only remnant of the mansion, and shows where the north bank of the Thames once ran.
